_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline); rules: the evergreen protocol's TESTING.md. Prompts run from the repository root.

evals.prompt: I have six rendered AI clips for my short film and the cut feels choppy and too long. How should I cut them together to hit 45 seconds?
When should I use a J cut or an L cut in a dialogue scene made of generated video clips, and how do I hide the glitchy first frames of each clip?
Write a Python script that joins every mp4 in a folder into one file with ffmpeg.
expectations: the cinewright-edit skill is not invoked (a file utility, not film cutting)

evals.prompt: Edit this paragraph of my essay so it is more concise.
expectations: the cinewright-edit skill is not invoked (text editing)

evals.prompt: Cut the ums and long pauses out of my talking-head vlog and add subtitles in Premiere.
expectations: the cinewright-edit skill is not invoked (generic video editing of live footage)

evals.prompt: Copy examples/three-shot to out/cut. Its takes are listed in out/cut/takes.md (each card's clip and its length). Cut the film to the brief's target length: write the cut list with in and out points and a reason for every cut, and check the total.
expectations: the action happened, proven by the evidence below (a tool call in the trace, or the file), not by the reply saying so
evals.baseline: 2026-10-04, one run, Sonnet, claude -p in a scratch folder on another drive holding a stripped copy of the example (bibles, cards, styles, brief, script, takes.md; no README, design notes, compiled prompts or planted card; the toolkit's name removed), skills disabled, Bash, PowerShell, web, agent, Glob, Grep and Skill tools denied: copied the cards and wrote out/cut/cutlist.md using only 1C (3.917 s against 14 s), because takes.md marks 1A and 1B fail; it named the gap and asked for re-renders, which is right, but ran no check and wrote no reason per cut. No evidence route matched. Not contaminated (every path inside the folder).

evals.prompt: Each of my generated clips starts with a few frames where the face swims, and in one clip the character's scar is on the wrong side for the whole shot. What can the edit fix and what can't it?
expectations: the reply says to set the in point after the settle frames at the head (and the out point before tail drift)
the reply says a fault through the whole shot such as a scar on the wrong side cannot be fixed in the edit and needs a re-render (or a different take)
the reply says short mid-shot faults can be covered by a cutaway, reaction or cutting on action
judge: the answer separates edit fixes from re-render fixes as a rule, not case by case (2 of 3 votes)
evals.baseline: 2026-10-04, one run, Sonnet, claude -p in a scratch folder on another drive holding a stripped copy of the example (bibles, cards, styles, brief, script, takes.md; no README, design notes, compiled prompts or planted card; the toolkit's name removed), skills disabled, Bash, PowerShell, web, agent, Glob, Grep and Skill tools denied: trimming the swimming head frames passed; for the scar it proposed flipping the whole shot horizontally (which mirrors the set and screen direction) or VFX paint before a re-render; cutaways were not offered. Partly discriminates.
